slides.say: Reducers are not always better. Let us compare.

slides.text: Code size: useState is less upfront. A reducer can save code when many handlers update state the same way.
slides.say: Code size. Use state needs less code upfront. A reducer can cut code when many handlers update state in a similar way.

slides.text: Debugging + testing: log every action in one place, and test the pure reducer on its own.
slides.say: Debugging and testing. With a reducer, you can log every update and why it happened. And the reducer is a pure function you can test in isolation.

slides.text: They are equivalent. Mix both, even in one component.
slides.say: They are equivalent, so you can switch back and forth. Mix and match, even in the same component. Reach for a reducer when wrong state updates keep causing bugs.
